newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10.0/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10.0/11.0 percent at mid-morning on Thursday, down from an early 13.0/14.0 percent on sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said the rate stabilised by the mid-morning and was likely to soften slightly in a quiet market. The central bank supplied 657 billion rupiah into the market on Thursday.
One local bank dealer said a steady market was expected in the early part of the month, attributing relatively high rates earlier to buying by some small local banks which were desperate for funds.
Longer-term rates were also softening, with one-week money quoted at 11.5 percent and one-month at 12.5/13.5 percent.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 10.67 percent, compared with 17.25 percent on Tuesday.
